A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLOSS and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite substantial rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, expert-selection and fusion ablations, domain-transfer results, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds transfer experiments, validation-set evaluations, computational measurements, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The core entropy-based selection, top-4 expert construction, and fusion equations remain unchanged. The new transfer experiment introduces a limited adaptation: target classes absent from the source vocabulary use the default WCLIP classifier (Section 5.1, Table 5).

E1.justification: The dataset roster remains unchanged. Table 5 adds a distinct transfer scenario from COCO-Stuff to Cityscapes, VOC20, and PC59 with partially overlapping vocabularies, extending the earlier transfer evaluations using shared driving-scene classes.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the benchmark, backbone, fusion, and expert-metric comparisons are retained. Added experiments use existing base models. Seg-TTO is newly discussed but is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds single-image OOD evaluation, transductive validation-set selection, selection using 5/25/50/75 validation images with evaluation on the remainder, common-class versus all-class scoring, and runtime/memory measurements. It also revises MaskCLIP's stated resizing/window/stride from 336 pixels (560 for Cityscapes)/224/112 to 448/448/224. The PDFs do not establish whether retained results were rerun under this revised description.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the original ablations, v2 examines low-data selection combined with domain shift, transfer across partially overlapping vocabularies, and validation-based selection. Appendix A.2 adds computational scaling analysis, while Appendix A.8 and Figure 16 add qualitative cases showing individual experts and their fused predictions.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages and standard deviations over 10 seeds for the low-data experiment in Figure 3. v2 introduces no additional repeated-run disclosure, uncertainty estimation procedure, or significance testing for its added evaluations.

E6.justification: v2 adds transfer, validation-selection, runtime/memory, and qualitative results. For example, the newly reported single-image OOD comparison averages 28.3 mIoU with FLOSS versus 26.4 without it (Table 4). In retained Table 1, the Cityscapes CLIP-DINOiser baseline changes from 31.1 to 31.3; the other matched benchmark and ablation tables retain their values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations are retained. Equation (8) merely makes explicit that the estimated expert-set size equals N. Average Probability and MaNo equations move from Section 5.2 to Appendix A.5, and the ITI formulation remains unchanged. No new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain training- and label-free template selection, entropy-based expert identification, expert fusion, and improvements across OVSS models, shifted datasets, and low-data settings. The rewritten abstract and additional experiments retain these core claims.

C2.justification: v1 describes computational overhead as minimal. v2 qualifies this in Section 4.2 and Appendix A.2, acknowledging substantial costs for larger class vocabularies and explaining NACLIP's Cityscapes preprocessing cost. It also interprets the new transfer and qualitative results as evidence of expert portability and complementary predictions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7 newly documents all 80 template strings and their order. Appendix A.2 provides resource measurements and specifies NACLIP's 1120-by-560 Cityscapes resolution and 36 overlapping crops. These expand documentation; the template bank and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Seg-TTO, citing De Silva et al.'s test-time optimization work and discussing its LLM-generated attributes for specialized domains. The remaining cited works and the positioning around unsupervised template selection are substantially retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related work are substantially rewritten and condensed. Low-data evaluation moves into the main results, metric formulations are consolidated in the supplement, and the expanded supplementary material moves before the references.

P2.justification: v2 adds dedicated transfer tables (4 and 5), the computational-cost table (8), and qualitative fusion panels (Figure 16). Results pages are rearranged, tables gain yellow highlighting, and several retained plots receive revised colors and labels. Existing appendix analyses are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the existing empirical contribution with targeted transfer and validation checks, clearer exposition, and an explicit template list. Its most useful correction is replacing unqualified minimal-overhead language with measured computational tradeoffs: Table 8 reports ADE20K CLIP-DINOiser inference increasing from 23 to 339 ms with FLOSS. These additions improve transparency and practical assessment while leaving the established method and principal conclusions largely intact.
